short_summary: Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro left Brazil for Florida after losing the presidential runoff to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and defying a court order to surrender his passports.

sources.title: Flavio Bolsonaro vanishes after Brazil election defeat, reportedly flees to US

paragraphs: Following a contentious runoff defeat in Brazil’s presidential election, far-right Senator Flávio Bolsonaro vanished from public view before surfacing in southern Florida. Bolsonaro touched down at Miami-Opa Locka Executive Airport on Wednesday morning alongside his wife and two teenage daughters, ending days of intense speculation regarding his whereabouts. His departure unfolded against the backdrop of an order from Brazil’s Supreme Federal Court instructing him to surrender his passports within twenty-four hours amid ongoing criminal inquiries. After Bolsonaro missed the deadline, authorities promptly cancelled his travel documents. Nevertheless, the senator managed to slip overland into neighboring Argentina before boarding a chartered jet bound for the United States.

The electoral contest concluded on Sunday with incumbent left-wing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva securing re-election with 51.79 percent of the vote against Bolsonaro’s 48.21 percent, a margin exceeding four million ballots. While Brazil’s electoral court, congressional leadership, and even Bolsonaro’s own political party formally validated the outcome, the defeated candidate echoed unsubstantiated allegations of electoral fraud and mathematical impossibility. In a contentious public letter issued after reaching Florida, Bolsonaro initially styled himself the "true president" before releasing an amended text identifying himself as "the leader of Brazil." Insisting that he had not fled but rather departed from a "regime of exception," he portrayed himself as the victim of political persecution and thanked Argentine President Javier Milei and Donald Trump for their support.

Bolsonaro’s clandestine journey began late Tuesday night when he crossed the border into Puerto Iguazú, Argentina, where Brazilian citizens can legally enter using domestic identity cards rather than passports. From there, the family boarded a Gulfstream IV private jet that stopped briefly in Guayaquil, Ecuador—reportedly to circumvent Brazilian airspace—before proceeding north to Florida. Upon arrival, a somber Bolsonaro, clad in a black bulletproof vest, was shielded by aides holding black umbrellas as he entered a waiting vehicle under police escort. No supporters were present to welcome him, and border agents kept roughly two dozen reporters at bay. The United States government furnished humanitarian visas, with President Trump confirming that officials had granted him a pass to enter the country.

Lula condemned Bolsonaro’s secretive exit as shameful during an event celebrating his eighty-first birthday, contending that figures with nothing to hide have nothing to fear. The departure closely mirrors that of the senator’s father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, who traveled to Florida in late 2022 before Lula’s inauguration and was later sentenced to twenty-seven years in prison for plotting a coup. Flávio Bolsonaro currently faces two pending Supreme Court investigations, one involving irregular transfers to a biographical film about his father and another examining an alleged money-laundering scheme connected to betting companies. With his eight-year Senate term and parliamentary immunity scheduled to lapse on January 31, it remains uncertain how long he intends to stay in the United States.

facts.fact: Flávio Bolsonaro lost the Brazilian presidential runoff election to incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, receiving 48.21% against Lula's 51.79%.

Following his defeat, Brazil's Supreme Court ordered Bolsonaro to surrender his passports within 24 hours amid ongoing corruption and money-laundering investigations, but he failed to comply, prompting authorities to cancel the documents.

Bolsonaro crossed into Argentina by land on Tuesday night, boarded a private Gulfstream jet in Puerto Iguazú, stopped briefly in Ecuador, and landed at Miami-Opa Locka Executive Airport on Wednesday morning.
The United States government granted visas to Bolsonaro and his family, with US President Donald Trump confirming they were given a pass to enter the country.

In a statement issued from the US, Bolsonaro repeated unsubstantiated claims of electoral fraud, labeled himself the leader of Brazil, and denied fleeing, asserting he left to escape political persecution.
President Lula criticized Bolsonaro's departure as shameful, while Bolsonaro's political party and Brazilian electoral authorities had already formally recognized Lula's victory.
